source_title: Mutational signature in colorectal cancer caused by genotoxic pks-positive Escherichia coli
evidence_model: human intestinal organoids and human tumor genomes
perturbation: exposure to genotoxic pks-positive E. coli and comparison with non-genotoxic controls
main_observation: colibactin-associated mutational patterns were reproduced in organoids and detected in human cancer genomes
key_limitation: molecular attribution is not a delivered therapeutic perturbation

source_title: Programmable conjugative CRISPR interference targeting genotoxin in the gut
evidence_model: multiple pks-positive strains and mouse CRC model
perturbation: conjugative delivery of dCas9 CRISPRi targeting colibactin biosynthetic genes
main_observation: reported reduction of genotoxicity DNA damage and tumorigenesis with preserved community diversity
key_limitation: non-peer-reviewed preprint and delivery/safety generalization remains unresolved

source_title: Bacteroides fragilis Toxin Coordinates a Pro-carcinogenic Inflammatory Cascade via Targeting of Colonic Epithelial Cells
evidence_model: ApcMin mice colonized with enterotoxigenic B. fragilis
perturbation: isogenic in-frame deletion of both bft-2 copies
main_observation: parental ETBF induced tumors while the delta-bft strain was indistinguishable from sham for tumor number
key_limitation: constructed-strain colonization does not demonstrate delivery to an established native microbiome

source_title: FadA promotes DNA damage and progression of Fusobacterium nucleatum-induced colorectal cancer through up-regulation of chk2
evidence_model: CRC cells and mouse colorectal tumor model
main_observation: FadA knockout reduced DNA damage and tumor number size and load relative to wild type
key_limitation: genetic knockout is not an in situ delivery experiment and the current metagenomic assay did not recover fadA

source_title: Fap2 Mediates Fusobacterium nucleatum Colorectal Adenocarcinoma Enrichment by Binding to Tumor-Expressed Gal-GalNAc
evidence_model: human CRC tissue binding and mouse tumor localization
perturbation: naturally Fap2-negative strains and inactivated Fap2 mutants
main_observation: Fap2 loss reduced binding to CRC cells and localization to established mouse tumors
key_limitation: target engagement and localization were tested more directly than tumor prevention; the current assay did not recover fap2

source_title: Secondary bile acid production by gut bacteria promotes Western diet-associated colorectal cancer
evidence_model: gnotobiotic CRC mouse models and human colon organoids
perturbation: baiH mutant Faecalicatena contorta unable to produce dehydroxylated secondary bile acids
main_observation: the mutant produced less DCA fewer colon tumors and less organoid proliferation than wild type
key_limitation: the causal mutant was not C. scindens and does not establish species-specific delivery
